You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Here every submission is a program instead of a grid. To submit, write a Python function transform(grid) that
returns the output grid for an input of this task, in one ```python block using only the standard library, and end
your reply with {"action": "submit"}. Your program is run on the test input and its output is submitted. Before that
it is checked, at no cost, on every demonstration pair you have for this task, and a failure is reported to you;
after 3 failed checks in an instance, a program's output is submitted without a check. A program that reproduces all
the pairs you have is kept for the task: when the task returns, it is run on the new test input first and its output
is submitted.

```python
def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    from collections import Counter

    bg = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]

    # If two rows agree up to a point and then one has a solid-color
    # continuation where the other has only background, fill the gap.
    for r1 in range(h):
        for r2 in range(r1 + 1, h):
            a, b = grid[r1], grid[r2]
            p = 0
            while p < w and a[p] == b[p]:
                p += 1
            if p == w or sum(v != bg for v in a[:p]) < 2:
                continue

            ta, tb = a[p:], b[p:]
            if all(v == bg for v in ta) and tb and len(set(tb)) == 1 and tb[0] != bg:
                for c in range(p, w):
                    out[r1][c] = 1
            elif all(v == bg for v in tb) and ta and len(set(ta)) == 1 and ta[0] != bg:
                for c in range(p, w):
                    out[r2][c] = 1

    # Repeated single horizontal runs may have differing right endpoints.
    runs = []
    for r, row in enumerate(grid):
        pos = [c for c, v in enumerate(row) if v != bg]
        if not pos:
            continue
        lo, hi = pos[0], pos[-1]
        color = row[lo]
        if all(row[c] == color for c in range(lo, hi + 1)):
            runs.append((r, lo, hi, color))

    # Group runs of the same color with closely aligned starting points.
    unused = set(range(len(runs)))
    while unused:
        seed = unused.pop()
        component = {seed}
        changed = True
        while changed:
            changed = False
            for i in list(unused):
                if any(runs[i][3] == runs[j][3] and abs(runs[i][1] - runs[j][1]) <= 1
                       for j in component):
                    component.add(i)
                    unused.remove(i)
                    changed = True
        end = max(runs[i][2] for i in component)
        for i in component:
            r, lo, hi, color = runs[i]
            for c in range(hi + 1, end + 1):
                if grid[r][c] == bg:
                    out[r][c] = 1

    return out
```
